vulnerabilities.description: AEAD suites are offered, but CBC suites are still accepted for older clients.
vulnerabilities.detail: A client limited to CBC suites falls back to MAC-then-encrypt constructions with known timing side channels.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Drop CBC suites once no client needs them.

analysis.detail: Observed directly by the collector on each affected asset.

vulnerabilities.description: The certificate's validity period has ended.
vulnerabilities.detail: Clients either fail closed (an outage) or are configured to ignore validation errors, which removes protection against impersonation.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Renew and deploy a new certificate; automate renewal (ACME, ACM, cert-manager).

analysis.detail: Observed directly by the collector on each affected asset.

vulnerabilities.description: The certificate is signed by its own key rather than a CA the clients trust.
vulnerabilities.detail: Clients must either pin it or skip validation; skipped validation allows man-in-the-middle impersonation.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Issue it from your internal or public CA and distribute that CA to clients.

analysis.detail: Observed directly by the collector on each affected asset.

vulnerabilities.description: The endpoint negotiates classical ECDHE/DHE only; no hybrid ML-KEM group (such as X25519MLKEM768) is offered.
vulnerabilities.detail: Traffic recorded today can be decrypted once a cryptographically relevant quantum computer exists (harvest now, decrypt later). This matters for data that must stay confidential beyond that horizon.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Offer a hybrid ML-KEM group first where the TLS stack supports it.

analysis.detail: Observed directly by the collector on each affected asset.

vulnerabilities.description: The endpoint only speaks deprecated protocol versions, so every connection uses broken or weak cryptography.
vulnerabilities.detail: Every session to this endpoint can be attacked with the weaknesses of the old protocol; modern clients will fail to connect.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Upgrade the TLS stack (or the appliance firmware) and enable TLS 1.2 and 1.3.

analysis.detail: Observed directly by the collector on each affected asset.

vulnerabilities.description: The endpoint accepts TLS 1.0, which RFC 8996 deprecated in 2021. It relies on SHA-1/MD5 in the handshake and CBC constructions with known attacks.
vulnerabilities.detail: A client that can be downgraded to TLS 1.0 is exposed to BEAST-style CBC attacks and to weak handshake hashes; regulators treat TLS 1.0 as a failed control.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Allow TLS 1.2 and 1.3 only. Check old clients first with the endpoint's access logs.

analysis.detail: Observed directly by the collector on each affected asset.

vulnerabilities.description: The endpoint accepts TLS 1.1, deprecated by RFC 8996 together with TLS 1.0.
vulnerabilities.detail: TLS 1.1 still uses MD5/SHA-1 in the handshake PRF and offers no AEAD ciphers; it keeps clients on a downgrade path.

analysis.detail: Observed directly by the collector on each affected asset.

vulnerabilities.description: The asset relies on RSA, elliptic-curve or Diffie-Hellman cryptography, which Shor's algorithm breaks on a large quantum computer.
vulnerabilities.detail: Data encrypted with these keys can be recorded now and decrypted later (harvest now, decrypt later); signatures can be forged once such a computer exists.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Add it to the PQC migration plan; prioritise by the Mosca score.

analysis.detail: Observed directly by the collector on each affected asset.

vulnerabilities.description: The RSA key is smaller than 2048 bits (below 112-bit security).
vulnerabilities.detail: RSA-1024 is within reach of well-funded attackers and is disallowed for new use; a recovered key lets an attacker impersonate or decrypt.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Replace with RSA-3072 or ECDSA P-256 (and plan the move to ML-DSA / ML-KEM).

analysis.detail: Observed directly by the collector on each affected asset.

vulnerabilities.description: The SSH server offers diffie-hellman-group14-sha1 or group-exchange-sha1.
vulnerabilities.detail: SHA-1 in the key exchange hash weakens the session's integrity guarantees; RFC 9142 recommends against these methods.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use curve25519-sha256 / diffie-hellman-group16-sha512 or a hybrid PQ method.

analysis.detail: Observed directly by the collector on each affected asset.

vulnerabilities.description: The SSH server offers HMAC-SHA1. HMAC-SHA1 is not broken, but SHA-1 is being retired and better options exist.
vulnerabilities.detail: No practical attack today; it is a crypto-agility and compliance gap.

analysis.detail: Observed directly by the collector on each affected asset.

vulnerabilities.description: The SSH server offers only classical key exchange (curve25519, ECDH, DH).
vulnerabilities.detail: Recorded SSH sessions (including file transfers and secrets typed into them) become readable once a large quantum computer exists.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Upgrade OpenSSH and prefer mlkem768x25519-sha256 or sntrup761x25519-sha512@openssh.com.

analysis.detail: Observed directly by the collector on each affected asset.

vulnerabilities.description: The endpoint accepts TLS_RSA_* suites, where the session key is encrypted with the server's long-term RSA key.
vulnerabilities.detail: Anyone who records traffic today and later obtains the server key (theft, legal demand or a future quantum computer) can decrypt every recorded session. Static RSA is also the precondition for Bleichenbacher/ROBOT padding oracles.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Remove TLS_RSA_* suites so every session uses ECDHE (forward secrecy).

analysis.detail: Observed directly by the collector on each affected asset.

vulnerabilities.description: The SSL protocol, as used in certain configurations in Microsoft Windows and Microsoft Internet Explorer, Mozilla Firefox, Google Chrome, Opera, and other products, encrypts data by using CBC mode with chained initialization vectors, which allows man-in-the-middle attackers to obtain plaintext HTTP headers via a blockwise chosen-boundary attack (BCBA) on an HTTPS session, in conjunction with JavaScript code that uses (1) the HTML5 WebSocket API, (2) the Java URLConnection API, or (3) the Silverlight WebClient API, aka a "BEAST" attack.

analysis.detail: Matched on: PROTO_TLS10 (finding type). A version or configuration match is not proof of exposure.
